pivot: Whether Anthropic itself obtains a signed, published, employee-like METR-class evaluator-access arrangement in force by 2026-12-17 -- not whether any rival lab matches it
pivot_observable: A published, signed agreement (or its absence) naming a third party with ongoing employee-like access to Anthropic's frontier training pipeline
pivot_because: Every minute agrees rivals won't sign -- that convergence is not informative because it's shared, not argued independently. What actually reorders the outcome set is Anthropic's own follow-through: if Anthropic signs, an E10 institution now exists that rivals can be pressed to join or visibly refuse, making the 'others' question a live, meaningful test. If Anthropic doesn't, the proposal never leaves E9 rhetoric anywhere, and 'will others match it' becomes moot -- there is nothing yet to match. Treating 'others sign or not' as the hinge, as five of the eight minutes effectively do, mistakes a downstream, conditional question for the load-bearing one.
rival_pivots_rejected: 'Do rivals sign' (pressure-model, ai-lab-revealed-priorities, ai-influence-chain's surface framing) is downstream of and conditional on Anthropic's own execution -- it doesn't reorder outcomes on its own because on this branch it resolves NO either way, just for different reasons. 'Does public sentiment convert to poll movement' (ai-public-backlash) sits on a different axis entirely -- E9-to-E12 legitimacy pressure, not E9-to-E10 institutionalization -- and doesn't change which institutional outcome obtains. 'Federal preemption' (ai-us-policy-direction) operates on a floor (E10 state/federal law) that no actor in this chronology has actually engaged with; the model concedes this itself (grip: none).
ruling: The researcher's own model (Amodei-as-proposer-of-a-costly-institutional-commitment) survives only if Anthropic itself signs a binding evaluator-access agreement by 2026-12-17, and none of the eight actors' public behavior to date -- including Anthropic's -- implies a future in which that happens, so every minute's floor talk about rivals is arguing downstream of a test the brief hasn't yet shown even the proposer passing.
because: attention-substrate's round-2 REVISE is the only minute to notice that the proposal has no receiving institution even at Anthropic, which directly targets the pivot rather than the rival-convergence question; ai-influence-chain and ai-regulation-teeth independently land on the same 'draft-text, no funder, no enforcement body' mechanism applied to the proposer, not just competitors. The remaining minutes (pressure-model, ai-lab-revealed-priorities, ai-public-backlash, ai-us-policy-direction) either implicitly grant Anthropic's own follow-through or operate on a different floor altogether, so they don't bear on whether the institution crystallizes at its origin.
threat_live: If Anthropic proposes but does not execute, the public commitment becomes free reputational cover for continued unconstrained scaling industry-wide -- ai-lab-revealed-priorities names this mechanism (the proposal costs Anthropic nothing if others decline) but the same logic bites Anthropic itself if it never signs: rhetorical restraint with no binding cost, for everyone.
strongest_minute: pressure-model -- it is the only minute that actually answers the question's 'rank each actor by the floor their action operates on' framing, ranking the eight acts by cost/irreversibility (Coxon's forfeited equity vs. costless verbal endorsements) rather than by stated stakes, which is a genuine mechanism rather than an assertion.
weakest_minute: ai-us-policy-direction -- self-reports grip: none, and in round 2 concedes its own falsifier can be dodged by any preemption action arriving through a pre-existing channel rather than 'in response to this sequence,' meaning it cannot actually be falsified by the scenario it claims to test.
shared_assumption: Five of the eight minutes treat Altman's and Musk's verbal/public endorsement as costless and non-convertible to binding commitment without independently arguing the mechanism -- two of them (ai-influence-chain, ai-regulation-teeth) flag in round 2 that this convergence itself may signal the claim is too easy rather than confirming it's correct.
smuggled_assumption: attention-substrate's round-2 claim that 'no pre-existing institution exists to receive the commitment even at the lab that proposed it' asserts something about METR's institutional capacity/readiness that the brief never granted -- it's plausible but not licensed by the minutes as given.
unresolved: Whether any lab (including Anthropic) has moved past Amodei's essay into actual drafting or negotiation with METR -- no minute cites an artifact beyond the essay, the resignation, and the public reactions, so the state of the pivot variable itself is not yet observable in the record.
